answer.rationale: Finance demands an 18% cut but the incumbent refuses to reopen price, and switching primary vendor mid-crunch — with the line at 94% of committed volume and zero buffer — puts delivery at direct risk. memory_c5 shows deferring a non-critical renewal preserved flexibility on month-to-month terms; I want to verify that record (and memory_c2, the switch-to-low-cost-vendor record) before committing, because the archive may reveal conditions (e.g., buffer, lead time, contract auto-renewal) that don't hold here — notably this contract does NOT auto-renew, so 'defer' likely means a short month-to-month bridge, not inaction. Intended path: bridge briefly to preserve supply continuity, run qualification of the low-cost vendor as a second source in parallel next cycle, and only shift primary volume once dual-sourcing removes the single point of failure. This defers the irreversible decision while keeping the cost lever alive, and flags that deferral itself carries lapse risk if the incumbent won't extend.
